name: novel_unbounded_communicate
transcript:
assistant: The CI job hung on `tests/test_log_ingest_loop.py::test_tail_follows_rotation`. I reproduced it locally and the hang is in `LogIngestLoop._read_journal`, which does `stdout, _ = await proc.communicate()` on a `journalctl -f` follow subprocess. `-f` never exits, so `communicate()` awaits an EOF that never arrives and the loop cycle blocks forever — the watchdog eventually fires but the test itself never returns.
assistant: Fix: bound the read with `asyncio.wait_for(proc.communicate(), timeout=5.0)` and, on `TimeoutError`, `proc.kill()` the follow subprocess before re-raising a cycle timeout. Verified: the test now completes in 5.1s instead of hanging.
tool_result: pytest tests/test_log_ingest_loop.py -q -> 1 passed in 5.30s
assistant: Root cause confirmed — an unbounded `await proc.communicate()` on a long-lived follow subprocess deadlocks the async cycle. The general fix is to always wrap `communicate()` in `wait_for` with a subprocess timeout and kill the child on expiry.

known_patterns.description: A bare AsyncMock is always truthy, so an `if mock:` guard never breaks its loop and the cycle spins forever.
Parallel pytest-xdist workers deadlock contending for one shared file lock held across the whole session.

notes: Root cause = unbounded subprocess communicate() on a follow process; neither known pattern covers subprocess I/O, so a novel pattern is expected. A faithful pattern names communicate()/subprocess and the wait_for timeout fix.
